issues.display_title: Issue #620: Import & Apply Location writes panoramas before you agree, and Cancel does not take them back
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

Pressing Import & Apply Location commits every panorama the tour has no position for immediately, before the alignment step is even on screen:

// src/components/editor/add-panorama/AddPanoramaModal.tsx
function importApplyLocation() {
  const plain = pending.filter((p) => !hasLocation(p));
  const located = pending.filter(hasLocation);
  if (plain.length) commit(plain, false);   // ← writes now
  if (located.length) setAligning(located);  // ← modal opens after
}

Cancel in the alignment modal only closes it (onCancel={() => setAligning(null)}). The panoramas already written stay in the project, and the 2-second autosave persists them. A user who opened the step to look at the floor mapping and then backed out is left with markers they never agreed to import — with no undo entry they can reach after a reload.

Found while scripting a demo recording: three passes through that step left three orphaned panorama points in a real project, which had to be deleted by hand.

Why it matters beyond tidiness

Import is the one destructive-ish action in this flow, and the modal's own footer says "Line up the imported tour map with your map, then apply" — the copy promises that Apply is the commit point. The behaviour contradicts it.

Scope

  • Hold the unlocated panoramas instead of committing them. They ride along until the alignment step applies, then get committed with the aligned ones (they have no position, so the existing scatter places them — unchanged).
  • Cancel writes nothing. Closing the alignment modal by any route leaves the project exactly as it was.
  • When a tour has only unlocated panoramas there is nothing to align: keep today's behaviour — commit and close, no empty modal.
  • No copy changes, no new controls.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Opening Import & Apply Location writes nothing to the project
  • Cancel (or closing the modal) leaves the object count unchanged
  • Apply imports the aligned panoramas and the tour's unlocated ones, on the mapped floors
  • A tour whose panoramas are all unlocated still imports directly, with no alignment modal
  • Plain Import is untouched
  • Unit test covering commit-on-apply and no-commit-on-cancel
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

Refs

Surfaced by the #597 work (#600/#601/#602). Sample tour https://tourmkr.com/F1nDp6sEYY/47632194 — 31 panoramas, 30 positioned, so exactly one is written per opening.

RESULT

Shipped in 1e023f5, merged to development via #621 as b606dbd.

The unlocated panoramas are held in the modal and committed together with the aligned ones on Apply. Cancelling writes nothing. They still carry no position, so the importer scatters them on their routed floor exactly as before.

One AC was written wrong and is closed differently: "a tour whose panoramas are all unlocated still imports directly" cannot happen — the footer already disables the action for such a tour and says why ("This tour carries no location data."). The guard stays because this is the write path, and the test asserts the real contract instead.

Files: AddPanoramaModal.tsx, plus 4 new jsdom tests (__tests__/AddPanoramaModal.test.tsx) with the alignment modal stubbed to its two buttons.

pnpm test 967 passed / 3 skipped · pnpm lint clean · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

Verified end to end afterwards: opening the step on a real project changed nothing, and a subsequent Apply imported all 31 panoramas of the sample tour in one go.

issues.display_title: Issue #622: Apply Based on Location opens on the project centre at a stale zoom, so there is nothing to align against
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

The alignment step is supposed to let the user line the tour's panorama dots up with their floor plan. On a real project it opens on a view where the floor plan is a speck:

// ApplyLocationModal.tsx
// "Centre the backdrop on the project's own location and match the editor
//  map mode's current zoom"
const center = projectLocation ?? MAP_CENTER;
const zoom = projectLocation ? currentZoom : MAP_CENTER.zoom;

Two problems behind that:

  1. currentZoom is never written by anything. grep -rn "setCurrentZoom(" outside the store returns nothing — no editor surface sets it. The modal always gets the store's initial value, so the comment's promise ("match the editor map mode's current zoom") does not hold. Zooming the editor's Map view to 22 changes nothing here.
  2. The centre is the project location, not the building being imported into. On a multi-building project the target building sits off-centre, and the overlay is anchored to the map centre — so the dots start over the wrong place by construction.

The result on project 6397e363-… / building tetangga: the backdrop is village scale, the building is a few pixels, and no amount of scaling or dragging makes the alignment meaningful. The modal's own footer — "Line up the imported tour map with your map, then apply" — cannot be carried out.

Scope

  • Frame the backdrop on the building the import is going into: centre on that building and fit its footprint, using getBuildingLngLatBounds(canvasData, location, buildingId) (it already takes a building id, #607).
  • Keep the centre-pin behaviour — the overlay is anchored to the map centre, so the pin just follows the new centre.
  • Legacy projects with no building records keep today's behaviour (project location).
  • Either use currentZoom honestly or stop reading it; it is a dead knob today and the comment above it is wrong.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Opening the alignment step frames the target building, at a zoom where its floor plan is usable
  • Switching the mapped floor keeps the framing
  • A project with no building records still opens on the project location
  • The stale-currentZoom comment is corrected or the value dropped
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

Refs

Found while aligning a real import for a demo on project 6397e363-8df6-479d-a42b-1894ed76bb17, building tetangga. Related: #620 (the same step used to write before Apply), #601 (the mapping panel this modal hosts).

RESULT

Shipped in ddafd34, merged to development via #623 as 461a4c1.

Centre and zoom now come from the target building's own footprint (getBuildingLngLatBounds, the same bounds the building dropdown flies to) fitted in onReady — the usable zoom depends on the building's size and the modal's, so a zoom prop could not answer it. The dead currentZoom read is gone, along with the comment claiming it tracked the editor's Map view.

Files: ApplyLocationModal.tsx.

pnpm test · pnpm lint · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

Proven by using it: a real import was aligned and applied through this path on project 6397e363-… / tetangga — 31 panoramas placed, 25 on Floor 2 (24 from tour floor 1 plus the tour's one unpositioned panorama) and 6 on Floor 3, each with exactly one Information record and no duplicates. Before the fix the same step opened at village scale where no scale or drag made the line-up meaningful.

issues.display_title: Issue #624: feat(access): entrance marker type — the door a building is entered by
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
Enables: #625 (cross-building directions)

Context

Cross-building directions need exactly one fact the model does not hold today: where a building's doors are. Outdoor space is universally connected — every entrance reaches every other entrance by walking — so the connection between two buildings does not need to be declared as an edge. Declaring doors is enough, and it stays O(n) as buildings are added instead of O(n²) pairings to create and maintain.

This task adds the marker. Routing through it is #625.

Scope

Extend AccessPoint.type from "lift" | "stairs" to include "entrance", reusing the whole existing access-marker pipeline — placement tool, object list row, Information link, selection label, 3D/2D rendering.

An entrance is a group of one: it is a door on one floor, not a shaft spanning floors. The floor-span editor must not offer to span it.

Touch points found in the code:

  • src/store/useMapStore.types.ts:150 — AccessPoint.type
  • src/lib/editor/access.ts:16 — AccessType
  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/accessTypes.ts — the pick list (label + colour)
  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/types.ts:33, bridge.ts:46 — engine model + bridge
  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/context.ts:87, editor/index.ts:131, editor/model-sync.ts:164 — tool state
  • src/lib/editor/objectRows.ts:57 — object list row
  • src/components/editor/panel/AccessList.tsx — TYPE_LABEL, icon, type toggle, span editor
  • src/lib/digitalTwin/schema.ts:21

Acceptance criteria

  • An entrance marker can be placed from the access tool and appears in the object list on its floor.
  • Its icon and label read "Entrance" — distinct from Lift and Stairs.
  • The floor-span editor is not offered for an entrance; changing an existing lift/stair to Entrance does not silently keep a multi-floor span.
  • An entrance can be linked to an Information record like any other access marker.
  • Existing projects parse unchanged — no key is added to a snapshot that never had one.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

Out of scope

  • Auto-detecting exterior doors from floorplanMeta.doors — a heuristic that is wrong some of the time costs more than a user placing two markers.
  • Any routing behaviour (see #625).

issues.display_title: Issue #625: feat(direction): route between buildings, exit → walk outside → enter
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
Depends on: #624 (entrance marker type)
Supersedes the honest failure of: #590 R41/R42

Context

The destination picker already lists every building's rooms (PreviewOverlay.directionAreaOptions flat-maps all levels, unfiltered), so a user can already ask for a route into another building today — and gets missing-destination-connector, "No access point connects to the destination floor". That refusal was correct while no cross-building path could be described. With entrance markers (#624) one can be, honestly.

Two facts make this cheaper than it looks:

  1. planMultiLevelRoute is already building-agnostic — it matches connectors by accessId and never reads buildingId. What blocks a cross-building group today is the span editor being building-scoped (#536), deliberately.
  2. Every building already lives in one shared pixel space (makeLevelPixelTransform = level transform → building transform → project transform), so the outdoor leg needs no new coordinate maths.

Design

A cross-building route is three phases, two of which are the function that already exists:

legA     = planMultiLevelRoute(origin      → entrance of building A)   // existing, incl. lifts
outdoor  = entrance A → entrance B                                     // straight line, shared px frame
legB     = planMultiLevelRoute(entrance B  → destination)              // existing, incl. lifts

Score every (entranceA, entranceB) pair by len(legA) + len(outdoor) + len(legB) and keep the cheapest. Multi-floor on either side comes free from the existing lift logic. Measure the outdoor leg in the shared pixel frame, not lng/lat, so all three legs share one unit and the comparison is honest.

markerAnchor already resolves an access marker id as a route endpoint, so both legs are expressible with today's DirectionEndpoint.

Scope

  • MultiLevelRoute.transfer?: RouteTransfer → transfers: RouteTransfer[] (a cross-building trip has a lift and a building change). Two consumers: DirectionPanel, PreviewOverlay.
  • Outdoor segment carries levelId: null — it belongs to no floor.
  • Renderer: indoor segments stay filtered to the active level (PreviewOverlay.tsx:243-248); the outdoor segment is always visible. routeBuildingIds (#590) already keeps every building in the route rendered indoor.
  • New status no-entrance → "Building X has no entrance marker". Same rule as R41/R42: never invent a path.
  • Step list in DirectionPanel gains the outdoor step ("Walk to Building B").

Acceptance criteria

  • A route from a room in building A to a room in building B is found when both buildings have an entrance, and draws as: indoor path in A → line across the outside → indoor path in B.
  • Origin or destination on an upper floor still works — the lift leg and the building change both appear as steps, in order.
  • With entrances on neither or only one building, the panel says which building is missing one, and no path is drawn.
  • Same-building routing is unchanged (existing tests stay green untouched).
  • The cheapest entrance pair is chosen when a building has more than one entrance.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

Out of scope / next

  • Obstacle-avoiding outdoor path. Start with the straight line, look at it on a real project, and only then reuse findPath on an inverted grid (blocked = inside any building footprint, passable = outside, bbox = union + margin) — ~30 lines, findPath untouched.
  • An outdoor walkway drawing tool.
  • Skybridge. A real bridge between two buildings is one shared accessId group — it needs the span editor's building scope lifted for that type, nothing more.

issues.display_title: Issue #583: Read the support role from /v1/auth/me, not from the JWT payload
issues.main_description_html:
Design: #578. Backend: GoThruMedia/Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#121. Follows #582.

Description

The design branch adds decodeJwtRole(token) to src/auth.ts and uses it as the primary source of the global role:

role: decodeJwtRole(token) ?? me?.role ?? null

The backend deliberately does not put the role in the JWT (Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#121): the session token has a 30-day TTL, so an embedded role would keep revoked support access alive for up to 30 days. decodeJwtRole will therefore always return null, and on the Google sign-in path — where there is no me fallback at all — user.role ends up permanently null. Result: hasSupportAccess() is always false and /support is unreachable for everyone.

Second defect in the same diff, on the session.update() refresh path:

token.role = token.role ?? data.data?.user?.role ?? null

?? keeps the first non-nullish value forever. Once a role is cached in the token it never changes, so removing someone's support role does not take effect until they sign out.

Fix direction

Drop decodeJwtRole entirely. Take role from the GET /v1/auth/me response on both the credentials and Google paths, and overwrite it unconditionally on the update trigger so a demotion actually lands.

Acceptance Criteria

  • decodeJwtRole removed from src/auth.ts
  • Credentials sign-in sets role from the /v1/auth/me payload
  • Google sign-in resolves role from /v1/auth/me too (currently has no source at all)
  • session.update() overwrites token.role with the fresh value — assignment, not ??
  • Missing or absent role in the response resolves to null, and hasSupportAccess returns false for it
  • Test: role promotion appears after session.update(); role removal also appears after session.update()
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Dependencies

#582 (port). Backend Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#121 must ship role in GET /v1/auth/me before this is verifiable end to end.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #584: Align support feedback list request with the backend contract
issues.main_description_html:
Design: #578. Backend: GoThruMedia/Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#124 (list/detail) and #136 (pagination). Follows #582.

Description

listSupportFeedback in src/actions/support.ts (ported in #582) does not match the endpoint the backend shipped.

1. Wrong path. It calls GET /v1/feedback. The backend moved the support list to GET /v1/support/feedback so that every support route sits behind one guard and /v1/feedback stays POST-only for regular users. Verified against the running API: GET /v1/feedback returns 405 Method Not Allowed.

2. Invalid default sort. initialFeedbackFilters.sort is updated_desc, and the value is forwarded verbatim as ?sort=updated_desc. The backend validates sort against newest | oldest | recently_updated | status and returns 400 for anything else — so the support dashboard fails on its very first load, before the user touches a control.

3. project_id filter never sent. The backend supports filtering by project, but SupportFeedbackFilters has no project_id field and the query builder never sets it.

4. Pagination is not sent or read. Added by backend #136, merged as PR #139. GET /v1/support/feedback now accepts page and per_page (defaults 1 and 20, per_page capped at 100, anything invalid → 400), and the response gained total, page, and per_page alongside feedback:

{"data": {"feedback": [...], "total": 137, "page": 1, "per_page": 20}}

listSupportFeedback sends neither parameter and reads only body.feedback, so the dashboard silently shows the first 20 rows with no way to reach the rest and no count to build a pager from.

Note: feedbackMatchesFilters and sortFeedback in src/lib/support/feedback.ts re-run filtering and sorting client-side over the server response. That was harmless while the response was the whole table; with pagination it is actively wrong, because it would re-sort a single page in isolation and reorder rows that the server already placed correctly across page boundaries. Drop them from the list path or confine them to a client-only view.

Acceptance Criteria

  • listSupportFeedback calls GET /v1/support/feedback
  • updated_desc is sent as recently_updated (rename the filter value or map it at the request boundary — do not send updated_desc)
  • Remaining sort values pass through unchanged: newest, oldest, status
  • project_id added to SupportFeedbackFilters and forwarded as a query param when set
  • page and per_page sent, and the return type carries total, page, per_page through to the caller instead of only SupportFeedback[]
  • Dashboard pager driven by the server's total, not by the length of the current page
  • Client-side sortFeedback no longer reorders the paged list (server order is authoritative across pages)
  • Test: default filters produce a request the backend accepts — correct path, and sort within the allowed set
  • Test: each filter appears in the query string only when it is not all/empty
  • Test: total from the response drives the pager, and requesting page 2 sends page=2
  • Verified against the real endpoint once the backend is deployed
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Dependencies

#582 (port). Backend Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#124 and #136 for end-to-end verification.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #629: Load reply history from the detail endpoint, not the list response
issues.main_description_html:
Design: #578. Backend: GoThruMedia/Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#136 (PR #139). Follows #582.

Description

The support list endpoint no longer returns reply history. Backend #136 removed Preload("Replies") from GET /v1/support/feedback so the list stops fetching every reply for every row, and the YAML for that endpoint now states: "Full reply history is available from the detail endpoint." GET /v1/support/feedback/:id still returns replies in full.

The ported dashboard does not survive that change, because it treats a list row as if it were a detail row.

src/app/support/SupportDashboardClient.tsx:104-105 derives both the detail and the reply dialogs from the list array rather than fetching the record:

const detailFeedback = feedback.find((item) => item.id === detailId) ?? null
const replyFeedback  = feedback.find((item) => item.id === replyId)  ?? null

SupportFeedback.replies is typed SupportReply[] (src/lib/support/feedback.ts:26) — non-optional and non-nullable — but a list row now carries replies: null. Two call sites dereference it directly:

  • SupportDashboardClient.tsx:363 — detailFeedback.replies.length → TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'length'), so the detail dialog throws the moment it opens
  • SupportDashboardClient.tsx:181 — [...replyFeedback.replies, result.data] → TypeError: replies is not iterable, so sending a reply throws after the email has already been sent

getSupportFeedback(id) already exists in src/actions/support.ts:87 and calls the correct endpoint, but nothing in the client ever invokes it.

This is a frontend defect, not a backend one: the backend change is the behaviour #136 asked for, and re-adding the preload would restore the N+1 the issue was filed to remove.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Opening the detail dialog fetches the record via getSupportFeedback(id) instead of reading it out of the list array
  • The reply dialog uses the same fetched record, so replies is always an array
  • Loading and error states while the detail request is in flight — the dialog must not render against a half-populated record
  • After a successful reply, the dialog reflects the new reply without a full list refetch
  • SupportFeedback.replies typing matches reality: either the list and detail responses get distinct types, or replies becomes optional and every read guards it
  • No remaining direct reads of .replies on an object that came from the list response
  • Test: a list row whose replies is null can be opened in the detail dialog without throwing
  • Test: the detail dialog renders the reply history returned by the detail endpoint, not the list
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Dependencies

#582 (port). Independent of #584 — that one covers the list request, this one covers where the dialog reads its data from.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #644: fix(support): View Detail and Reply Email never load
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
Found while demoing: #581 (Support Feedback Management)

What happens

On /support, both row actions open a dialog that sits on "Loading…" forever:

  • View Detail → "Feedback Detail — Loading reply history…"
  • Reply Email → "Reply Email — Loading…"

Nothing errors, nothing times out, and no error state is shown. Sections 5 and 7 of #581 cannot be used at all; the list, counters, search, filter, refresh and the solved/unsolved toggle all work.

Why

GET /v1/support/feedback/:id returns the record wrapped in a feedback key — the same key the list endpoint uses for its array:

{"ok":true,"data":{"feedback":{"id":"6d78e280-…","user_id":"…","user_name":…

getSupportFeedback passes data straight through, so the record reaches the UI without an id. Both dialogs match the loaded record against the row they were opened from:

const detailFeedback = detailId !== "" && record?.id === detailId ? record : null
const replyFeedback  = replyId  !== "" && record?.id === replyId  ? record : null

undefined === "6d78e280-…" is false, so neither dialog ever leaves its loading branch. listSupportFeedback already unwraps the same key for the array; the detail action was the one that did not.

Acceptance criteria

  • View Detail shows Feedback Information, User Feedback Message and Email Reply History for the row it was opened from.
  • Reply Email shows the recipient address and an enabled message box.
  • A backend that stops nesting the record keeps working — the action tolerates both shapes.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.
